goldens.comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:17 — Tunnel startup failures call cleanup and exit 0, so automated webhook verification can report success without a usable tunnel.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. Looking at lines 47-51 of the script, when a rate limit is hit, the script calls `cleanup` which executes `exit 0` (line 18). This means the script exits with success status code 0 even though the tunnel failed to start. In automated CI/CD or verification scenarios, this would incorrectly indicate success when the tunnel is not usable. The cleanup function at line 18 always does `exit 0` regardless of whether the tunnel was successfully established or failed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:43 — Deleting a cache never invalidates the connectedCalendars query, so the menu continues to show stale cache status until an unrelated refetch.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the deleteCacheMutation in CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx (lines 43-51), the onSuccess callback only shows a toast and calls onSuccess?.(). It does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query. In contrast, the disconnectMutation (lines 53-66) has an onSettled callback that explicitly calls utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate(). Since the cacheUpdatedAt is fetched from the connectedCalendars query (as shown in connectedCalendars.handler.ts), after deleting the cache, the UI will still show the old cacheUpdatedAt value until something else triggers a refetch. This is a real bug where the cache status display becomes stale after deletion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:9 — Existing cache rows are backfilled with the migration time rather than their actual cache-write time, so the new status can report stale entries as freshly updated.

adjudication.rationale: The migration adds `updatedAt` column with `DEFAULT NOW()`, meaning all existing CalendarCache rows will have their updatedAt set to the migration execution time rather than when the cache was actually written. The new UI feature (CredentialActionsDropdown) displays this timestamp as 'Last updated: {timestamp}' to users, which would incorrectly show stale cache entries as freshly updated. This is a data correctness issue that affects user-facing information.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1024 — This empty-data update repurposes SelectedCalendar.updatedAt yet the new cache-status path reads CalendarCache.updatedAt, leaving a misleading write with no consumer.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in CalendarService.ts line 1024, there's a call to `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` with an empty data object. Looking at the repository method in selectedCalendar.ts, this will trigger an updateMany with empty data, which in Prisma will update the `updatedAt` field due to @updatedAt directive. However, the cache status display in connectedCalendars.handler.ts reads from `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` which queries `CalendarCache.updatedAt`, not `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. This is a legitimate architectural concern - the write to SelectedCalendar.updatedAt appears to have no consumer in the new cache status feature, making it a misleading/dead write. This is not a bug per se (the cache status feature works via CalendarCache.updatedAt which has @updatedAt and gets updated on cache writes), but it's a valid code quality concern about orphaned logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:28 — Deleting cache rows bypasses the existing CalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential abstraction and its mock/feature-disabled behavior, duplicating persistence policy at the route boundary.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. Looking at the diff, deleteCache.handler.ts at line 28 uses `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })` directly, while the codebase has a CalendarCacheRepository with a `deleteManyByCredential` method (visible in calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts which logs 'Skipping deleteManyByCredential due to calendar-cache being disabled'). This means the new handler bypasses the repository abstraction and its mock behavior for when calendar-cache is disabled. This is a legitimate architectural concern - the handler should use the repository pattern for consistency and to respect feature flags.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:174 — Cache-status aggregation scans every cache row for each credential because the new query has no credentialId/updatedAt index, and expired cache entries are never pruned.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` method that uses `groupBy` on `credentialId` with a `where` clause filtering by `credentialIds`. While the query does filter by credentialId (so it's not scanning ALL rows), the finding raises a valid architectural concern: there's no index shown for the new `updatedAt` column added in the migration, and the `_max` aggregation on `updatedAt` could be slow without proper indexing. Additionally, the point about expired cache entries never being pruned is a legitimate concern - the diff shows cache entries have `expiresAt` but there's no cleanup mechanism visible. However, the claim that it 'scans every cache row for each credential' is somewhat exaggerated since the `where` clause does filter. This is a valid performance/architecture concern but not a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1024 — Every cache refresh rewrites updatedAt on every SelectedCalendar for the credential, creating write and lock amplification proportional to all event-type calendar selections.

adjudication.rationale: The diff at line 1024 shows `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` being called after every cache refresh. Looking at the repository method in selectedCalendar.ts, this updates ALL SelectedCalendar rows matching the credentialId. The finding correctly identifies that this creates write amplification - every cache refresh triggers updates to potentially many rows. While this is intentional (to track cache freshness), it's a valid architectural concern about database write load that scales with the number of calendar selections per credential. This is not a bug (it works as designed) but is a legitimate performance/scalability concern grounded in the actual diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:16 — No automated test covers the new destructive cache-deletion mutation’s ownership guard and credential-scoped deletion.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new deleteCache.handler.ts with a destructive mutation that deletes calendar cache data. This handler includes an ownership guard (checking credential belongs to user) and performs credential-scoped deletion. The finding correctly identifies that no test file is included in the diff for this new functionality. This is a legitimate concern for a destructive operation with security implications (ownership verification). The finding is specific, cites the exact file and line, and addresses real code added in the diff.
